newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-Atlantic spot power prices flat to lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-Atlantic spot power prices flat to lower.

text.p: Spot electricity prices in the U.S. Mid-Atlantic finished Monday mostly flat to lower from Friday amid cool weather and modest power demand.

Delayed returns of a couple of nuclear power plants in the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnect pool district from refueling did offset the bearish effect of lower usage, brokers and marketers said.
"The (generation) rates were surprisingly high," said a PJM trader, adding expensive oil and natural gas-fired stations needed to produce more power to compensate for the postponed unit startups.

Industry sources said a loop flow problem south of the PECO Energy Co's system forced hourly prices of PJM power up to the $40 a megawatt hour mark. The loop flow situation had little effect beyond the hourly scheduling.
The problem was linked to the return of the 1,055 megawatt (MW) Limerick nuclear unit 2 in Pottstown, Pa., to full power last week and ongoing outage of a major substation, they said.
Pennsylvania Power & Light Co postponed the startup of the 1,090 MW Susquehanna 1 nuclear power plant in Berwick, Pa., to Tuesday from Sunday to repair safety relief valve.
Duquesne Light Co delayed the restart of 833 MW Beaver Valley unit 2 in Shippingsport, Pa., by about five weeks from October 14.
Firm, peak electricity for Tuesday delivery at PJM was quoted at $21.50-$22.50 a MWh, down from Friday's range of $22.50-$23.00. Deals were heard done at $21.50, $21.75 and $22.00.
Firm, peak PJM power for the rest of the week was assessed at $22.00-$22.50, lower than Friday's $22.25-$23.35 quote.
November PJM electricity was pegged at $22.90-$23.25, slightly higher than $22.75-$23.00 on Friday.
December PJM power was mostly talked at $27.50-$27.75, a tighter range than Friday's $27.00-$27.60.
January/February 1997 PJM was unchanged at $31.25-$31.75. First-quarter 1997 PJM was pegged at $29.10-$29.50, up from Friday's $29.00-$29.20.
Second-quarter 1997 PJM deliveries were valued at $21.75-$21.85, flat from Friday's level.
July/August 1997 PJM electricity was again thinly discussed in the $31.00-$31.35.
